newsitem.title: UK: Mother Teresa pleading to die, newspaper says.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa pleading to die, newspaper says.

text.p: Mother Teresa, the 86-year-old nun adored around the world for her work with the poor, has begged doctors to let her die, a British newspaper reported.
Mother Teresa is currently being treated in a Calcutta clinic for heart disease but longs to die in peace, the Independent newspaper quoted a former colleague as saying.
"She talked very openly about not wanting to live any longer," it quoted Jim Towey, a former seminarian with Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity order, as saying.
Towey, who now heads a foundation in Florida dedicated to the dignity of the elderly and dying, said he had spoken to Mother Teresa regularly by telephone.
"She's helped so many people to die that she can accept mortality much better than her doctors," he added.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the poor, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989.
She was admitted to the clinic on Friday after she showed an irregular heartbeat.

Doctors said they were waiting to see if she needed a test known as an angiography, in which X-rays and an opaque dye are used to find blocked arteries. Such a test could show if she needs more surgery.
She has been treated for blocked arteries twice -- in the United States in 1991 and in Calcutta in 1993.
Doctors said on Wednesday her condition had improved slightly with no breathing problems or chest pain.
"Mother herself is not all that concerned about it," Towey told the newspaper. "After all, she's got one foot in heaven."
